solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police burst out, seizing Conservative government business

indicators.note: the jumbled letters seize, or take hold of, the abbreviation inside them
letters that are out are in disarray, so the words police burst are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers break out of somewhere and grab a Tory, all in the course of official state work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POLICE BURST, and 'seizing' puts C inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The state-run part of the economy, as opposed to private enterprise, is the business done by and for government.

clue.text: Ring up twitching colleague to see how words are pronounced?

parts.note: to ring someone up is to phone them
a twitch is a tic, an involuntary spasm
a colleague or associate is an ally

explanation.surface: Calling a co-worker who has a nervous twitch, perhaps to check how to say something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' looks like an adjective on the colleague but supplies the noun TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing or spelling something according to its sounds is describing it by its pronunciation; the question mark marks the loose adverbial phrasing.

clue.text: Located while in sleeping place

indicators.note: the word for while sits inside the sleeping place

parts.note: a bed is where one sleeps
as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'

explanation.surface: Someone is found while they are in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be situated or stationed somewhere is to be headquartered there, a synonym of positioned.

clue.text: Occupying street, perhaps a worker's moment

parts.note: occupying a place is being in it
a worker ant is one kind of ant, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A labourer takes a brief break while out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' points to the insect caste, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A very brief point in time, as in 'wait an instant', is a synonym of a moment.

clue.text: Tin contains insipid part of flower

indicators.note: the symbol for tin holds the word for insipid inside it

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
tame can mean dull or insipid

explanation.surface: A tin can holds some bland piece of a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-producing male organ of a bloom is one of its structures, an example of a floral part.

clue.text: Stand-up maybe needing company microphone

parts.note: mic is a short form of microphone

explanation.surface: A stand-up performer needs a troupe and a mic for the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian is one example of a funny performer, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: How to put weight on each in public

indicators.note: the abbreviation for each sits within the word for public

parts.note: overt means open or public

explanation.surface: Advice on gaining weight by eating in front of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming more food than needed is the way people gain pounds, so the phrase describes the method.

clue.text: Easy to understand addict at pre-season match?

parts.note: a drug user is an addict
a friendly is a non-competitive game, often played before the football season starts

explanation.surface: A drug addict turns up at a warm-up football game.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly is a match that counts for nothing, as British football clubs play in pre-season.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designed to be simple to operate or follow for ordinary people is easy to understand.

clue.text: Buried in Truro, a sister's fertile patch

indicators.note: the letters lie buried within the run of words Truro, a sister's

explanation.surface: A sister has a green, productive spot tucked away in the Cornish city of Truro.
explanation.definitionFit: A green, watered spot in a desert is a fertile area surrounded by barren land.

clue.text: Melissa wanders, lacking purpose

indicators.note: letters that wander move about, so the name Melissa is rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Melissa drifts about without any goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no aim or direction means being without purpose.

clue.text: Kill grouse etc, when ultimate strategy comes into play

definitions.text: when ultimate strategy comes into play

parts.note: to end something is to kill it off
grouse and similar birds shot for sport are game

explanation.surface: Shooting grouse and the like is the hunter's final tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stage of a chess game, or any contest, is the phase where closing tactics decide the outcome.

clue.text: Shout approval of revolutionary meeting Queen

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crosswords' favourite revolutionary
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: People applaud a revolutionary meeting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout encouragement or praise, as a crowd does, is a synonym of applauding vocally.

clue.text: Dreadful pun — it's making contributions

indicators.note: a dreadful version is a mangled one, so pun and it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's terrible wordplay is what they are adding to the conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Things put in to a project or discussion, such as ideas or resources, are contributions.

clue.text: Highly desirable era for feathers

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A wonderful period in history for feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's covering of feathers taken together is its plumage.

clue.text: Film shown in Bratislava: Tarzan

indicators.note: the title is shown within the run of letters of Bratislava: Tarzan

explanation.surface: A Tarzan movie is being screened in the Slovak capital.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster is an example of a film.

clue.text: Vessel I'm able to show palace in Rome

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids
I am able is I can

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can display a container at a Roman residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's residence and seat of government lies within Rome, so it is a palace there.

clue.text: Emotional problem to end conversation abruptly

definitions.meaning: a psychological fixation or neurosis that bothers someone
to put the phone down suddenly on someone

explanation.surface: A troubled person cuts a chat short.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a neurotic fixation; the phrasal verb is replacing the receiver to terminate a call.

clue.text: Lincoln possibly admitting American ill-treatment

indicators.note: the name lets the abbreviation in, holding it inside

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname; possibly because other Abes exist

explanation.surface: President Lincoln perhaps confesses to mistreating someone from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel or harmful handling of a person is mistreatment, a synonym.

clue.text: With a final twist, goes out live

indicators.note: the final pair of letters are twisted round, swapping their order

parts.note: exits means goes out

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a live show, with a surprise twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a final twist' turns round only the last two letters of EXITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive or have being is a synonym of to live.

clue.text: Insiders from party listen for performer

indicators.note: the insides of each word, without their outer letters, are taken

explanation.surface: People in the know at a party pay attention to an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer, dancer or other stage entertainer is a performer, especially in variety.

clue.text: Drop bombs on second place of torment

parts.note: hell is the place of eternal torment

explanation.surface: Bombing raids turn a spot into a second hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard with artillery or explosives is to pound a target.

clue.text: Doing some housework, ignoring initial inclination

indicators.note: the first letter of the housework word is ignored and dropped

parts.note: cleaning is doing housework

explanation.surface: Someone tidying the house skips the first step, inclined to slack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency or preference towards something is a bias or inclination.

clue.text: Set of beliefs about marsh plant

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
a reed is a plant of wet marshy ground

explanation.surface: A doctrine concerning a plant growing in a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious or political creed is a system of principles a group holds.

clue.text: Severe punishment, unusual type halted around North America

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation
an unusual arrangement of the words type halted is an anagram

explanation.surface: A harsh sentence, of an odd kind, stopped across the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TYPE HALTED and 'around' wraps those letters around NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution as a judicial sentence is the harshest possible penalty.
